results.corrected_title: FBI arrests OpenAI engineer accused of planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room
results.corrected_summary: Federal prosecutors have charged Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who had worked on OpenAI's product team since July 2025, with attempting to intercept oral communications. On 30 September, OpenAI staff found a covert audio recording device plugged into the USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room at the San Francisco office. FBI agents arrested him on Friday 9 October, and the case became public on 13 October. FBI Director Kash Patel said the aim was to capture sensitive communications about the company's superintelligence technology. OpenAI fired him and says it has no indication that he accessed or exfiltrated model weights.
key_facts: Suspect: Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, Saudi national, at OpenAI (product team) since July 2025
Device found 30 September 2026 in an executive conference room in San Francisco, plugged into the USB port of a TV; reportedly installed around 28 September
Arrested Friday 9 October 2026; the charge was made public 13 October (Northern District of California)
Charged with attempting to intercept oral communications; TechCrunch reports up to five years in prison
Kash Patel: the goal was to 'capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology'
OpenAI fired him and says it has no indications he accessed or exfiltrated model weights
results.issues: Core facts confirmed. CNBC returned 403. OpenAI's statement covers model weights only; the claim about source code or customer data was dropped. The charge is a complaint, not a conviction.

results.corrected_title: Accenture caps company-funded Claude use at $29 per employee per month
results.corrected_summary: According to an internal memo reported by 404 Media on 15 October 2026, Accenture told many employees it will centrally fund only $29 of Claude usage per person per month. Some employees had been spending up to $1,000 a month, largely on agentic Claude Code work. Usage above the cap must be charged to a project or team budget that agrees to pay for it. 404 Media presents this as part of a wider trend of companies curbing employee AI use as token costs grow quickly.
key_facts: Cap: $29 per employee per month in centrally funded Claude usage
Some employees had previously spent up to $1,000 per month
Usage above the cap must be charged to a project or team budget (WBS code); the memo says licences may be reassessed
Reported by 404 Media (Joseph Cox) on 15 October 2026; several outlets say the policy took effect 1 October
An Accenture spokesperson said the firm provides 'the right tool for the right work' and continues to invest in AI
results.issues: 404 Media is paywalled; only the introduction was readable. $29, $1,000 and the wider-trend framing are confirmed there. Effective date and project-budget mechanism come from secondary coverage. It is a soft cap, not a hard ceiling.

results.corrected_title: Anthropic signs its first Canadian data centre lease with EverWind in Nova Scotia
results.corrected_summary: On 16 October 2026, Anthropic signed a long-term lease (reported by Reuters as 20 years) with EverWind for the first 95 MW phase of a planned data centre campus at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia. It is Anthropic's first data centre deal in Canada. EverWind's overall plan is worth more than C$10 billion: about C$8 billion for the campus and C$2 billion for wind power. Phase one is targeted for late 2027, with a 325 MW expansion planned for 2028 (420 MW in total). The value of the lease was not disclosed, and the linked wind farms will not be ready when phase one opens.
key_facts: Anthropic's first data centre agreement in Canada, with EverWind Fuels at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia
First phase is 95 MW, targeted for late 2027; a 325 MW second phase is planned for 2028, subject to conditions (420 MW combined)
EverWind's total plan is more than C$10 billion (about C$8 billion campus plus C$2 billion wind)
Lease term reported as 20 years (Reuters); the lease value was not disclosed
The four linked wind farms will not be finished when phase one opens; EverWind and Anthropic pledged to cover grid costs so existing customers' rates do not rise
results.issues: Core claims confirmed. The Globe and Mail says only 'long-term lease'; the 20-year term comes from Reuters-based coverage. The Bloomberg URL was not opened (paywalled).
